clue.text: 7 could be on one working list!

parts.note: a machine that is working is running or functioning, i.e. operating
a table is a list of figures or items set out in order

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the 7 might feature on some active roster.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' points to the answer at 7-across, a patient paying for their own care, who could well lie on the thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery is carried out on this piece of hospital furniture, so a patient lies on it during an operation.

clue.text: Prevaricate, accepting fine and sentence, for example

indicators.note: one word taking in another, so the fib-telling verb holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to prevaricate is to tell an untruth, i.e. to lie
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Someone evasive is fined and given a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole-of-life prison term is called a life sentence, so it is one example of a sentence.

clue.text: Down's up, and hearts race

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: feeling down means feeling sad
H is the card-players' abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A cheerful lift from gloom, and pulses quicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down's up' reads as 'Down is up': SAD written upwards gives DAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a short sprint, a quick run.

clue.text: Cloudy and strangely unable to start raining

indicators.note: letters arranged strangely are set out in an odd new order
the opening letter of the word raining is taken

explanation.surface: Overcast weather, oddly failing to start a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' makes NEBULA out of UNABLE; 'to start' adds R from raining.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebular describes something like a nebula, a hazy interstellar cloud, so it means misty or cloud-like.

clue.text: Patter that places this loosely

indicators.note: letters held loosely are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A salesman's spiel that sets things out in a casual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' rearranges PLACES THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Patter is the smooth persuasive talk a seller uses to win a sale.

clue.text: Covers ducks in blue — no, the opposite!

indicators.note: the surface says ducks go in blue, but 'no, the opposite' reverses the instruction so blue goes in ducks

parts.note: eiders are large sea ducks
feeling blue means feeling down

explanation.surface: Bedding with ducks in blue, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no, the opposite!' flips the surface order of 'ducks in blue', so the blue piece goes inside the ducks instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Eiderdowns are quilts that are spread over a bed as covers.

clue.text: One pays for treatment for soldier with calm

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
patient means calm and willing to wait

explanation.surface: A self-funded hospital case who is a serene squaddie.
explanation.definitionFit: A private patient is someone who pays a doctor or hospital directly rather than using state care.

clue.text: Areas of the country where society supports temperament and reticence

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the others

parts.note: a person's nature is their character or temperament
reserve is restraint or reticence in manner

explanation.surface: Rural spots where polite society values a calm disposition and restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts S at the foot of the down entry, under NATURE and RESERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: These are protected stretches of countryside set aside for wildlife.

clue.text: Sign put on eco-friendly nursery building

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: green means environmentally friendly
in astrology each zodiac sign rules a house

explanation.surface: A notice fixed to a sustainable children's nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursery' is a plant nursery, not a creche; 'put on' places the zodiac word after the eco word.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass structure where young plants are raised under shelter.

clue.text: Woman born to want endlessly

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, having no end

parts.note: a want is a need

explanation.surface: A woman born to crave without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for 'born', introduces a married woman's maiden name.

clue.text: The wheatsheaf serves food!

indicators.note: the pub name serves up some of its own letters, which lie inside it

explanation.surface: A pub called the Wheatsheaf offers meals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wheatsheaf is a common British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food or a meal.

clue.text: Master spiers is out of alternatives

indicators.note: every other letter of the word spiers is taken, the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A head spy has run out of other options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiers' are people who spy; take its 1st, 3rd and 5th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the respectful form of address to a master or gentleman.

clue.text: Letter maps out how to cast a shadow on the way

definitions.text: how to cast a shadow on the way

indicators.note: letters put out are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A letter lays out a route showing how to darken a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LETTER MAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp on a post lights the road at night, so things on it throw shadows.

clue.text: Thinking that if on time it's a worry

indicators.note: to worry something is to shake it about, so these letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A thought that being punctual is a concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worry' rearranges ON TIME IT'S A.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimation is judgement or opinion, the way one is thinking about something.

clue.text: Graft in factory after time was managed to the second

indicators.note: the factory word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a business that was managed was run, i.e. ran
a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: Hard work in a mill once time was run to the last second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graft' looks like British slang for hard work; here it is surgical tissue moved from one place to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical graft is tissue or an organ moved into a new site in the body.

clue.text: Terrible anger after final demand

indicators.note: the anger word follows the picked letter
the last letter of the word demand is picked

parts.note: ire means anger

explanation.surface: Fury follows a last-warning bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final demand' looks like an unpaid bill reminder; it gives only D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful or very bad.

clue.text: First to show approval thus

explanation.surface: The first step in signing off on something.
explanation.walkthrough: To initial a document is to add one's initials to it, a way of approving it.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first or opening; as a verb, to mark a paper with the opening letters of one's name.

clue.text: Guardian backing the Tory left! A discontented read

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the wets were the moderate, left-leaning wing of Thatcher's Conservative Party

indicators.note: the word read loses its contents, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Guardian reader supporting the Conservative left finds it an unhappy read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the moderate-Tory word round. 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward looks after property or people on behalf of others, a keeper.

clue.text: Hormone that will mostly offend at home

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to offend is to insult
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A gland secretion that will largely upset a household.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas releases this hormone to control blood sugar.

clue.text: Staunch supporter — the early move taking the leaders!

indicators.note: the leading letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A loyal backer praises an early decisive move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like an adjective, loyal; it is the verb, to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to stop or check it.

clue.text: To put together tense with shy is silly

indicators.note: silly letters are foolishly mixed up

explanation.surface: Combining nervousness with timidity is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges TENSE SHY IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To synthesise is to combine elements into a whole.

clue.text: Vision you once backed with energy

indicators.note: backed means turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned dream supported with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye is the organ of sight, so it stands for one's sight.

clue.text: The measure of power given a person elected

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, elected to the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Gauging influence after someone wins office.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampere is the unit of electric current, which an electrician measures alongside power.

clue.text: Neighbour with some brass coming back

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tuba is one of the brass instruments

explanation.surface: A neighbour returns with a few brass instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neighbour' is the verb here: to border on.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to lie next to or border on something.

clue.text: Buns galore are served in these places

indicators.note: food served up is dished out, so these letters are dished out anew

explanation.surface: Plenty of buns are dished up in these venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are served' rearranges BUNS GALORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lounge bars are the more comfortable rooms of a British pub, where snacks may be sold.

clue.text: Turn quiet? Fancy that!

parts.note: your turn in a game is your go
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone asked to take their turn silently exclaims in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: Offer including new tie

indicators.note: one piece includes another, holding it inside

parts.note: a bid is an offer at auction

explanation.surface: A bid for a brand-new necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind is to tie up or fasten.

clue.text: Survey that concerns a sea in dispute

indicators.note: letters in dispute are argued over and pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: A survey of matters involving a contested sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in dispute' looks like the indicator, but 'in' is fodder; 'dispute' rearranges CONCERNS A SEA IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnaissance is a military survey of ground to gather information.
